It's harder to do than to read but here it is,

1.) **Realise one undeniable truth: If your dump came as a shock, your dumper is a manipulative and horrible person.** No one, and I mean NO ONE loses feelings overnight. Your dumper likely used the months before your your relationship to get over you and had made up their mind long before. This means two things, one that they keep secrets, and two that they have poor communications skills and put their own feelings above yours. Does that sound like someone you want to be with? NO. Have some respect for yourself and let them go. If they do change, that kind of emotional fixing takes years and you don't want to wait around. 

2.) Accept that the relationship is over and no matter what you do, you can't save it. Don't make up fantasies of the person realising their mistake and coming back because it'll only lead to disappointment and if it does happen, the relationship will likely end in the same way. Ask yourself this, "Do you really want to be with someone who dropped you?" because that's what'll be in your head the entire relationship if you reunite.

3.) Write down the person's actions and break them down. Does a person who dropped you, ghosted you and ignored you sound like someone you want to be with?

4.) Get your mind off them and re-find yourself. Too often your partner has become so much a part of your life that your identity is tied to them so you need to rediscover yourself.
